# PanPan Marine

> PanPan Marine (operated by Guangzhou PanPanTech Co., Ltd., Guangzhou, China) supplies underwater inspection ROVs, long-distance tunnel inspection ROVs, underwater cleaning robots and dredging robots for water infrastructure: dams, hydropower tunnels, penstocks, intakes, trash racks, sumps, bridge piers and ports. Equipment is manufactured by Boya Gongdao (ROBOOCEAN). Contact: panda@panpantechnology.com.

Key facts:
- All figures below are manufacturer figures (brochure or official site) and should be confirmed for the supplied version.
- Manufacturer project references are projects in China completed by the manufacturer, not by PanPan Marine.
- Quotations are itemised per project; no list prices are published.

## Equipment
- [R-30 Compact Underwater Inspection ROV](https://www.panpanmarine.com/equipment/r-30-inspection-rov/): The R-30 is a compact, tethered underwater inspection ROV. Manufacturer figures: 21 kg vehicle weight, 300 m depth rating, 3 kg payload and a 1080p camera with 4× optical zoom and ±90° tilt. It suits visual inspection of dams, intakes and submerged structures where small size and easy handling matter.
- [R-45 Inspection ROV with 8 kg Payload](https://www.panpanmarine.com/equipment/r-45-inspection-rov/): The R-45 is a tethered inspection ROV with a larger payload allowance than the R-30. Manufacturer figures: 42 kg vehicle weight, 350 m depth rating, 8 kg payload and a 1080p camera with 4× optical zoom. It suits dam, intake and structure inspection that needs sonar, positioning or tooling on board.
- [AD-400 Long-Distance Tunnel Inspection ROV](https://www.panpanmarine.com/equipment/ad-400-tunnel-inspection-rov/): The AD-400 is a long-distance ROV for inspecting flooded water-conveyance and headrace tunnels. Manufacturer figures: 5 km maximum operating distance (official site; brochure 5.5 km), 1,000 m depth rating, 300 kg vehicle, 4K forward and 1080p rear cameras, with external tethered power.
- [A-80 Underwater Crawler Cleaning Robot](https://www.panpanmarine.com/equipment/a-80-cleaning-robot/): The A-80 is a floating and wall-crawling underwater robot for contact cleaning of trash racks, intakes and submerged surfaces. Manufacturer figures: 100 kg vehicle weight, 300 m depth rating, 15 kg payload and two HD cameras, with brush or cavitation water-jet cleaning modules and external tethered power.
- [AD-100 Underwater Dredging Robot for Sumps](https://www.panpanmarine.com/equipment/ad-100-dredging-robot/): The AD-100 is a remotely operated dredging robot for removing sediment from hydropower sumps and other confined submerged spaces. Manufacturer figures: 100 kg vehicle, 815 × 620 × 690 mm, six thrusters and front and rear cameras. It works as one system with a pump, discharge line and mud-water separation unit.
- [Compare all models](https://www.panpanmarine.com/equipment/compare/): side-by-side specifications for R-30, R-45, AD-400, A-80 and AD-100.

## Applications
- [Industrial Underwater Inspection ROVs](https://www.panpanmarine.com/solutions/industrial-underwater-inspection/): An industrial underwater inspection ROV replaces diver inspection of intakes, dams and submerged structures with a remotely operated camera and sensor platform. Choose it around the result you need: the R-30 for compact visual work, the R-45 when sonar, positioning or tools add payload.
- [Underwater Tunnel Inspection ROVs](https://www.panpanmarine.com/solutions/underwater-tunnel-inspection/): Long-distance underwater tunnel inspection uses a specialised ROV to travel kilometres through flooded headrace and water-conveyance tunnels. The AD-400 is designed for this task, with a 5 km official operating range. Success depends on route geometry, tether management, position referencing and a recovery plan.
- [Underwater Trash Rack Cleaning Robots](https://www.panpanmarine.com/solutions/underwater-trash-rack-cleaning/): Robotic trash rack cleaning uses a wall-crawling underwater robot to remove adhered deposits and fouling from intake racks without divers or draining. The A-80 carries brush or cavitation water-jet modules. It suits surface deposits; logs and large debris need a separate raking method.
- [Sump Cleaning & Underwater Dredging Robots](https://www.panpanmarine.com/solutions/underwater-sump-cleaning/): Robotic sump cleaning uses a remotely operated dredging robot to remove sediment from submerged sumps, replacing manual confined-space work with remote operation. The AD-100 works with a pump, discharge line and mud-water separation unit. Sediment properties, access and conveyance distance decide the system design.
- [Underwater Dam Inspection ROVs](https://www.panpanmarine.com/solutions/underwater-dam-inspection/): Underwater dam inspection with an ROV records the condition of the upstream face, intakes, gates and toe without putting divers in the water. Choose the vehicle around depth, visibility and the features to record: a compact ROV such as the R-30 for visual work, or the higher-payload R-45 when sonar and positioning are required.
- [Penstock Inspection Robots & ROVs](https://www.panpanmarine.com/solutions/penstock-inspection/): Penstock inspection robots must handle steep gradients, bends and long enclosed routes. For long flooded conduits, a long-distance tunnel ROV such as the AD-400 is the starting point; shorter accessible sections may suit an inspection ROV like the R-45. Plan the tether, position reference and recovery for the actual profile.
- [Bridge Pier & Port Underwater Inspection](https://www.panpanmarine.com/solutions/bridge-pier-port-inspection/): Bridge pier and port structure inspection with an ROV records scour, concrete damage, corrosion and marine growth below the waterline without diving. A compact ROV such as the R-30 can be launched from a quay or small boat; add imaging sonar for turbid water, and plan the work around current and tide.

## Buying guides
- [Underwater Dam Inspection with ROVs: A Planning Guide](https://www.panpanmarine.com/blog/underwater-dam-inspection-rov-guide/): An underwater dam inspection with an ROV records the upstream face, joints, intakes, gates, trash racks and the toe without putting divers in the water. Plan it around the features to record, reservoir visibility, depth and flow at intakes. Use a compact ROV for visual work and a higher-payload ROV when sonar and positioning are needed.
- [ROV vs Diver for Underwater Inspection: How to Decide](https://www.panpanmarine.com/blog/rov-vs-diver-underwater-inspection/): Use an ROV when the inspection is mainly visual or acoustic, when water is deep, long, enclosed or near intakes, or when the work repeats regularly. Use divers when the task needs hands-on work, tactile assessment or tools an ROV cannot carry. Many owners combine both: an ROV survey first, then targeted diver work only where it is needed.
- [Inspection ROV Cost: What Drives the Price of an Underwater ROV](https://www.panpanmarine.com/blog/inspection-rov-cost-guide/): The price of an inspection ROV depends far more on the complete configuration than on the vehicle alone. The main drivers are the vehicle class and depth rating, the sensors (especially sonar and positioning), tether length and reel, tools, training, spares and support. Compare quotations on an itemised, like-for-like scope and on cost over the inspection programme.
- [Underwater Cleaning vs Dredging: Choosing the Right System](https://www.panpanmarine.com/blog/underwater-cleaning-vs-dredging/): Choose underwater cleaning when the required result is removing deposits from a submerged surface. Consider dredging when the task is collecting and transferring accumulated sediment. Some sites need both. Specify the material, access, required result and complete supporting system before selecting a robot: the attachment, pump, hoses, separation equipment and handling arrangements can determine whether the proposed configuration is suitable.
- [How to Choose an Industrial Inspection ROV](https://www.panpanmarine.com/blog/industrial-inspection-rov-selection-guide/): Choose an industrial inspection ROV by defining the evidence your inspection must produce, then checking visibility, access, depth, flow, integrated sensors and recovery. Compare the complete field system, including its tether, control station, power, training and support. Shortlist a platform only when the supplier can demonstrate the proposed configuration against your task and provide a clear, itemized quotation.
- [Flooded Tunnel Inspection: A Procurement Planning Guide](https://www.panpanmarine.com/blog/flooded-tunnel-inspection-procurement-guide/): To procure a flooded tunnel inspection system, define the inspection result first, then compare the complete vehicle, sensing, tether, power, positioning and recovery package against your actual tunnel. Require sample deliverables, a stated configuration, site assumptions and an agreed acceptance plan before comparing prices. A manufacturer's maximum range is a starting specification; it does not establish usable coverage, defect-location accuracy or recoverability in your tunnel.
